tex_content.html:
If a three-dimensional $\kappa $-solution has a compact asymptotic gradient shrinking soliton, then it is isomorphic to a time shift of that soliton.
Proof

\sketch ↗ claim:compact-positive-curvature-round The asymptotic soliton is round. Smooth convergence makes the rescaled original slices increasingly pinched; scale invariance and Hamilton–Ivey pinching force every original slice to be round. A round flow is determined, up to isomorphism, by its manifold and singular time, so only a time shift remains.

□
